sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Detailed study guide and resources for Administration are currently being prepared. Check back soon for comprehensive explanations, summary diagrams, and expert preparation recommendations.

Key Dimensions of Study:

  • Definition, scope, and foundational theories.
  • Relevance to General Studies Paper & Contemporary contexts.
  • Core applications and structural framework.

practiceQuestions.q: During the Delhi Sultanate, which department was headed by the 'Diwan-i-Arz'?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Diwan-i-Arz was the military department of the Delhi Sultanate, originally established by Balban to safeguard the state from internal and external threats. The officer in charge was called Ariz-i-Mumalik. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following Sultans of Delhi introduced the system of branding horses (Dag) and maintaining descriptive rolls of soldiers (Chehra)?
practiceQuestions.sol: Alauddin Khalji instituted strict military reforms, including the 'Dag' (branding of horses) system to prevent substitution of war-horses and 'Chehra' (descriptive roll of individual soldiers) to prevent corruption. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India / NCERT]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the primary function of the 'Muhtasib' during the Delhi Sultanate and Mughal period?
opts: Censor of public morals and enforcer of Sharia
Chief judge of the imperial court
practiceQuestions.sol: The Muhtasib served as a public censor whose duty was to ensure that people lived according to the rules of Sharia, check weights and measures, and prevent public nuisances. [Primary Reference: Abul Fazl, Ain-i-Akbari / NCERT Medieval History]

practiceQuestions.q: In the administrative vocabulary of the Delhi Sultanate, what did the term 'Iqta' signify?
opts: A revenue assignment given to nobles or officers
A royal decree issued by the Sultan
practiceQuestions.sol: An Iqta was a territorial assignment given by the Sultan to nobles and military commanders in lieu of cash salary. The holder was called an Iqtadar or Muqti. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7 Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: Which Mughal Emperor instituted the 'Mansabdari System'?
practiceQuestions.sol: Akbar instituted the Mansabdari system around 1570-71 CE to organize the nobility, civil administration, and military forces into a single graded hierarchical structure. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Medieval India / Satish Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: In the Mansabdari system, what did 'Zat' and 'Sawar' denote?
opts: Zat denoted personal rank/salary, and Sawar denoted the number of horsemen to be maintained
Zat denoted military rank, and Sawar denoted infantry troops
Zat denoted revenue assignment, and Sawar denoted tax collection rights
Zat denoted religious status, and Sawar denoted civil administrative duties
practiceQuestions.sol: The Jat rank fixed the personal status and salary of a mansabdar, while the Sawar rank indicated the actual number of horsemen the mansabdar was required to maintain. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History / Ain-i-Akbari]

practiceQuestions.q: During the Mughal period, what was 'Zabt' or 'Dahsala' system associated with?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Dahsala (ten-year) system was introduced under Raja Todar Mal, under which average yields and prices of crops calculated over the past ten years were used as the basis for land revenue assessment. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval History]

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the chief judicial officer under the Mughal administration, second only to the Emperor?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Qazi-ul-Quzat was the highest judicial officer of the empire, responsible for administering justice, although the Emperor remained the fountainhead of justice. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: In the administrative division of the Mughal Empire, what was a 'Suba' headed by?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Mughal Empire was divided into provinces known as Subas, which were governed by a Subadar (also known as Sipahsalar or Nazim). Subas were further divided into Sarkars. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7 History / Ain-i-Akbari]

practiceQuestions.q: Which Vijaynagara administrative term refers to the territorial units or provinces?
practiceQuestions.sol: In the Vijayanagara Empire, the empire was divided into provinces called Mandalams or Rajyams, which were governed by Mandalesvaras. Mandalams were further subdivided into Nadus, Sthalas, and villages. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Muhammad bin Tughluq's administrative experiments, particularly the transfer of capital to Daulatabad, reflect systemic governance challenges?
opts: It demonstrated a visionary decentralization model that permanently stabilized southern borders.
It exposed the logistical failure of commanding a vast empire from a central pivot without considering geographical and communications constraints.
It successfully replaced agrarian taxation with urban mercantile taxes across all provinces.
It was primarily a religious migration to purge Delhi of orthodox Sufi orders.
practiceQuestions.sol: Muhammad bin Tughluq's shifting of the capital to Daulatabad was aimed at better control over the Deccan, but the forced evacuation of Delhi and the vast logistical hardships showed a disconnect between policy conceptualization and ground realities. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India / NCERT]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the core structural objective behind Sher Shah Suri's currency and administrative reforms, particularly the introduction of the 'Rupiya'?
opts: To standardise currency weights and foster commercial integration across a unified fiscal regime.
To eliminate all forms of land revenue and replace it exclusively with maritime trade tariffs.
To fund nomadic Mongol incursions through bullion hoarding.
To decentralize administrative power completely by delegating minting rights to village headmen.
practiceQuestions.sol: Sher Shah Suri introduced a silver coin of a standard weight (178 grains) called the Rupiya. This standardization of currency, along with the standardisation of weights and measures and road construction (Grand Trunk Road), was designed to facilitate trade and revenue collection. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7 History / Satish Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the Jagirdari system under the Mughals function in relation to the Mansabdari system?
opts: Jagirs were permanent hereditary estates granted independently of military ranks.
Jagirs were revenue assignments given to mansabdars in lieu of cash salaries, subject to periodic transfers.
Jagirdars were autonomous chieftains who paid no allegiance or revenue to the Mughal emperor.
Jagirdari was exclusively a religious grant system managed by the Sadr-us-Sudur.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Mansabdari and Jagirdari systems were complementary. While Mansab determined rank and salary, Jagir was the revenue assignment from which the mansabdar collected revenue to pay his troops and maintain his lifestyle. Frequent transfers prevented local entrenchment. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History / Satish Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of the 'Nayankara' system in the Vijayanagara administrative framework?
opts: It was a central taxation system exclusively for maritime ports.
It was a military feudal arrangement where military chiefs (Nayaks) were assigned territory (Amaram) in exchange for troops and tribute.
It was a religious endowment system managed by temple priests.
It was a judicial committee established to resolve caste disputes.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Nayankara system was the distinct administrative system of Vijayanagara where Nayaks (military chiefs) controlled tracts of land called Amaram and were obligated to maintain a specific military force and pay annual tribute to the central king. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the 'Ayyangar' system operate at the village level in the Vijayanagara Empire?
opts: A group of 12 hereditary village functionaries managed village affairs independently of central oversight.
It was an assembly of Buddhist monks overseeing local charities.
It was a tax-collecting agency operated solely by foreign merchants.
It was a judicial tribunal appointed directly by the Sultan of Madurai.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Ayyangar system involved a body of 12 functional officers (such as Karnam, Talari, etc.) who were granted tax-free land (manyam) to run village administration, maintaining continuity even during political upheavals at the center. [Primary Reference: Standard Historical Canon / Upinder Singh]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the fundamental difference between the 'Khalisa' lands and 'Jagir' lands under the Mughal administration?
opts: Khalisa lands were barren lands used for military drills, while Jagir lands were fertile agricultural plots.
Khalisa revenue went directly to the imperial treasury, whereas Jagir revenue was assigned to mansabdars for their upkeep.
Khalisa lands were owned by religious saints, while Jagir lands belonged to foreign ambassadors.
There was no administrative difference; the terms were used interchangeably.
practiceQuestions.sol: Khalisa was the crown land whose revenue was collected directly for the imperial treasury to meet central expenses, while Jagir lands were assigned to nobles (mansabdars) in lieu of their salaries. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History / Ain-i-Akbari]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Firoz Shah Tughluq's administrative approach differ from that of Alauddin Khalji regarding revenue and land grants?
opts: Firoz Shah centralised all power and abolished all military checks, while Alauddin promoted feudal lords.
Firoz Shah reversed Alauddin's centralising policies by reviving the Iqta system, making revenue assignments hereditary, and writing off peasant debts.
Firoz Shah introduced cash salaries for all soldiers, completely banning land grants, unlike Alauddin.
Both emperors followed identical economic policies without any divergence.
practiceQuestions.sol: While Alauddin Khalji sought to curb the power of nobles and restricted assignment grants, Firoz Shah Tughluq appeased the nobility and army by making Iqtas hereditary, abandoning branding (dag), and offering concessions. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: What role did the 'Waqia-navis' and 'Waqia-nigar' play in the Mughal administrative intelligence network?
opts: They were court poets responsible for chronicling imperial genealogies.
They served as official news reporters and intelligence agents who recorded events and reported directly to the center.
They were treasurers responsible for auditing provincial accounts.
They were religious scholars in charge of issuing fatwas.
practiceQuestions.sol: Waqia-navis and Waqia-nigar were intelligence reporters and news-writers stationed in provinces, cities, and courts to send regular reports of occurrences to the central imperial administration, maintaining checks on provincial officials. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra / Mughal Administration]

practiceQuestions.q: Why was the 'Bahamani' administrative structure influenced heavily by the Persian model of governance?
opts: Because the Bahamani founders and administrators heavily recruited Persian officials, scholars, and soldiers (Afaqi faction).
Due to a direct political merger between the Delhi Sultanate and the Persian Empire.
As a result of a papal decree mandating Persian administration in South Asia.
Because local Indian administrative techniques were entirely absent in the Deccan.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Bahamani kingdom drew heavily upon Persian administrative practices due to the influx of immigrants from Iran and Iraq (known as Afaqis), who brought Persian court culture, revenue administration styles, and military tactics. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the administrative significance of the 'Sadr-us-Sudur' in the Mughal imperial hierarchy?
opts: He managed foreign diplomatic relations with Safavid Persia and Ottoman Turkey.
He was the minister in charge of ecclesiastical and charitable endowments, overseeing grants to scholars and holy men.
He commanded the imperial artillery and naval fleets.
He functioned as the chief auditor for provincial trade taxes.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Sadr-us-Sudur acted as the head of the religious department, acting as an advisor to the emperor on religious matters and managing grants of tax-free land (Madad-i-maash or suyurghal) to pious men, scholars, and religious institutions. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History / Ain-i-Akbari]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the administration of the Delhi Sultanate:
1. The 'Diwan-i-Riyasat' was established by Alauddin Khalji to regulate the market and control commodity prices.
2. The 'Diwan-i-Khairat' was a specialized department created by Muhammad bin Tughluq for managing imperial slaves.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Alauddin Khalji set up the Diwan-i-Riyasat and Shahana-i-Mandi to enforce market controls and price regulations. Statement 2 is incorrect: Diwan-i-Khairat (Department of Charity) and Diwan-i-Bandagan (Department of Slaves) were established by Firoz Shah Tughluq, not Muhammad bin Tughluq. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Mughal Mansabdari System:
1. The Mansabdari system was hereditary, meaning the son of a mansabdar automatically inherited his father's exact rank and zat.
2. The Emperor could increase or decrease a mansabdar's rank based on performance and loyalty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Mansabdari system was not inherently hereditary; mansabs lapsed upon the death or dismissal of the holder, and sons had to start afresh, though sons of nobles were given initial favors. Statement 2 is correct: Ranks were bestowed, modified, or revoked entirely at the pleasure of the Emperor. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History / Satish Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Sher Shah Suri's administrative measures:
1. He reorganized the army and instituted the practice of branding horses, which was later adopted and refined by the Mughals.
2. He introduced copper coins called 'Dam', which became widely popular in rural trade.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: The branding of horses (Dag and Chehra) was originally instituted by Alauddin Khalji during the Delhi Sultanate, though Sher Shah also maintained strict military discipline. Statement 2 is correct: Sher Shah introduced the copper 'Dam' alongside the silver 'Rupiya', which formed the backbone of everyday rural commerce and taxation. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7 History / Satish Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the local administration of the Mughal Empire:
1. The Empire was divided into Subas, which were further subdivided into Sarkars, Parganas (or Mahals), and villages.
2. The 'Faujdar' was the chief executive and military officer of a Sarkar, responsible for maintaining law and order.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Mughal administrative hierarchy cascaded from Suba (province) to Sarkar (district), Pargana (sub-district), and Gram (village). At the Sarkar level, the Faujdar looked after military and executive duties while the Amalguzar looked after revenue. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Vijayanagara central administration:
1. The King was assisted by a Council of Ministers headed by a prime minister (Mahapradhani).
2. The administration lacked any codified civil or criminal legal system, relying purely on arbitrary royal decrees.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The King of Vijayanagara exercised absolute authority but was aided by a council of ministers and a prime minister (Mahapradhani). Statement 2 is incorrect: Justice was administered according to established customary laws, caste traditions, and Hindu jurisprudence, rather than arbitrary decrees alone. [Primary Reference: Nilakanta Sastry, A History of South India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Mughal land revenue systems:
1. Under the 'Batalai' or crop-sharing system, the state's share was fixed as a direct proportion of the actual produce at harvest time.
2. The 'Naskq' or Kankut system involved an estimation of revenue based on inspection and past yields without physical division of crops.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are accurate descriptions of Mughal agrarian revenue methods. Batalai (batai) was direct crop sharing in three forms (Khet-batai, Lang-batai, Batai-bhaoli), while Kankut/Nasq involved assessing standing crops or past averages to estimate state demand without immediate division. [Primary Reference: Abul Fazl, Ain-i-Akbari / Satish Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the administrative machinery of the Delhi Sultanate:
1. The 'Barid-i-Mumalik' was the head of the state intelligence and postal department.
2. The 'Diwan-i-Insha' handled the royal correspondence and drafted royal farmans.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Barid-i-Mumalik managed the spy network and postal couriers across the Sultanate, while the Diwan-i-Insha managed state correspondence, royal decrees, and communications between the center and provincial governors. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7 History / Satish Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Akbar's administrative reforms:
1. Akbar abolished the Jizya tax on non-Muslims in 1564.
2. Akbar introduced the 'Ahadi' troops, who were elite gentlemen-troopers directly recruited and supervised by the Emperor himself.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Akbar abolished Jizya in 1564 as part of his liberal religious and administrative measures. Ahadis were elite imperial troops (gentlemen troopers) who did not serve under any mansabdar but were directly under the command of the Mughal Emperor. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History / Ain-i-Akbari]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the revenue officials of the Mughal administration:
1. The 'Qanungo' was a hereditary revenue official at the pargana level who maintained records of land revenue rolls and local customs.
2. The 'Karori' was an officer appointed by Akbar to collect a crore of dams in revenue and audit provincial accounts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Qanungo maintained agrarian and revenue records at the pargana level. Karoris were introduced by Akbar in 1574-75 to maximize revenue collection, with each expected to collect one crore dams of revenue. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India / NCERT]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the administration of the Delhi Sultanate and Mughal Empire:
1. The office of the 'Vazir' in the Delhi Sultanate initially held supreme financial and political authority, which was later bifurcated under the Mughals into distinct portfolios like Diwan and Mir Bakshi.
2. The Mughals maintained a standing central army entirely free from the reliance on contingent troops supplied by mansabdars.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The Sultanate Vazir was all-powerful, but Mughal emperors bifurcated administrative duties, keeping finance under Diwan-i-Kul and military administration under Mir Bakshi. Statement 2 is incorrect: The Mughal army was largely feudal in structure; the bulk of the military forces (Sawar contingents) were brought and maintained by individual mansabdars, supplemented by standing royal troops (Ahadis and royal musketeers). [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History / Satish Chandra]
